title: Claude Code modeled 120 Low-Poly wrecks from reference photos - then shot its own Unity trailer!
author: _AssetSmithy_
selftext:
Claude Code made this trailer. It connected to Blender via MCP and wrote Python that modeled every wreck from reference photos of real cars and street objects. Then it built the scene, moved it to Unity 6 URP and rendered the video frame by frame. My part was direction and feedback: I reviewed contact sheets and sent things back, seven rounds until the style was right.  
  
What Claude Code built:  
\- 120 low poly wrecks and road props (64 models plus burnt-out, color and on-blocks variants), 288 to 9,854 triangles each  
\- 313 doors, hoods, trunks and tailgates with working pivots and Open/Close animations  
\- One shared 2048 texture atlas, painted by script  
\- The scene in Blender, plus lighting, smoke and fire from a baked fluid simulation in Unity  
\- The camera moves and the render: Unity in batch mode, every frame piped into ffmpeg  
\- FBX/GLB exports and ready packages for Unity and Godot, test-imported in both engines  
  
Not by Claude Code: the background mountains (TripoAI), the ground textures (Gemini/Flow) and the music (Suno).  
  
Ask me anything about the workflow. What would you improve?
